choices.label: A
choices.text: Evaluate effective capabilities and permissions rather than relying on the group name.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the account from only the Domain Administrators group.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Treat the account as nonadministrative because its group name does not contain “admin.”

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rename the group so that auditors can identify it as privileged.

explanation:
Administrative status is determined by the effective rights, privileges, and permissions an account can exercise. A group renamed `notadmin` can still provide administrative capability.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: it evaluates the real security capability; B — removing one obvious group membership may leave equivalent rights elsewhere; C — nomenclature does not determine effective privilege; D — renaming changes visibility, not capability.

Objective: Account & Privilege Monitoring & Authentication

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 104-105; Course MD PDF Page(s) 665-666; CM lines 20577-20622.
question: During an access review, an account in a group named `notadmin` has the same effective user rights and NTFS permissions as members of the organization’s administrator group. What is the best monitoring conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The account is not actually an administrator.

choices.label: B
choices.text: UAC is causing processes to run with reduced privileges by default.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every process from an administrator account already has full administrative privileges.

choices.label: D
choices.text: UAC changes the account’s group membership whenever the program starts.

explanation:
With UAC enabled, an administrator account’s processes run with reduced privileges by default and require intentional elevation for higher-risk actions. This limits the immediate impact of a compromised unelevated process.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — the account can still be an administrator; B — correct: it describes UAC’s default behavior; C — UAC specifically prevents every process from receiving full administrative privilege automatically; D — UAC does not change group membership.

Objective: Account & Privilege Monitoring & Authentication

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 127; Course MD PDF Page(s) 688; CM lines 21287-21307.
question: An administrator reports that a program launched from an administrator account cannot modify a protected system setting until the user explicitly elevates it. How should an analyst interpret this observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Require users to change the password more often while keeping password-only login.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Synchronize one complex administrator password across all systems.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add strong authentication such as multifactor authentication.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable authentication logging to reduce exposure of credential data.

explanation:
The course identifies password-only authentication as insufficient in the modern threat environment. Adding strong authentication, such as MFA, addresses a weakness that password length and rotation alone cannot remove.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — stronger passwords still leave a password-only scheme; B — synchronized administrator passwords expand the impact of compromise; C — correct: strong authentication adds another protection factor; D — removing authentication logs weakens monitoring rather than authentication.

Objective: Account & Privilege Monitoring & Authentication

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 135; Course MD PDF Page(s) 696; CM lines 21483-21502.
question: A company is redesigning authentication for an internal application that currently accepts only a password. Which change most directly addresses the course’s concern with password-only authentication?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Social engineering through a client-side exploit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Denial-of-service botnet activity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Certificate-pinning failure during TLS inspection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pass-the-hash, aided by unsalted and synchronized account hashes.

explanation:
Pass-the-hash uses a compromised Windows hash for authentication instead of requiring the cleartext password. Unsalted hashes and synchronized credentials make the same hash useful for pivoting to other systems.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — social engineering may enable initial access but does not explain hash-based remote logon; B — DDoS concerns availability, not NTLM hash authentication; C — certificate pinning is unrelated to NTLM; D — correct: it matches the observed hash reuse and remote logons.

Objective: Account & Privilege Monitoring & Authentication

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 170; Course MD PDF Page(s) 731; CM lines 22617-22646.
question: An analyst observes remote Windows logons that succeed when a compromised NTLM hash is supplied, even though the user’s cleartext password was never entered. The same username and hash are present on several systems. Which technique best explains the activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Service-side exploitation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Client-side exploitation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pass-the-hash.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Threat hunting.

explanation:
Service-side exploitation sends exploit data to a vulnerable listening service on the victim. It does not require a user to visit a site or execute a file.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: the vulnerable listening service and direct delivery match the definition; B — client-side exploitation requires victim interaction; C — pass-the-hash uses compromised credentials, not a listening-service exploit; D — threat hunting is a defensive activity, not an attack technique.

Objective: Attack Techniques

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 40; Course MD PDF Page(s) 42; CM lines 1289-1311.
question: An internet host sends exploit data directly to a public web server’s vulnerable listening service. No user interaction is needed for the exploit to reach the target. Which attack technique is being observed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A service-side exploit against a listening server.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Client-side exploitation using social engineering.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A false positive caused by a network IPS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configuration drift in a secure baseline.

explanation:
Client-side exploitation depends on interaction by the victim, such as visiting a site or downloading and executing a binary. Social engineering is commonly used to obtain that interaction.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — a direct attack on a server listener is service-side exploitation; B — correct: the user’s action is the defining clue; C — an IPS false positive is a defensive sensor event; D — configuration drift is a monitoring issue, not the access path.

Objective: Attack Techniques

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 68-69; Course MD PDF Page(s) 70-71; CM lines 2083-2119.
question: A user is persuaded to visit an attacker-controlled site and execute a downloaded binary. Which description best fits the initial access path?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Perimeter packet filtering.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Static firewall inspection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Advanced post-exploitation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Secure baseline auditing.

explanation:
Using a compromised host’s CPU, storage, bandwidth, or email account after initial access is advanced post-exploitation. The course emphasizes that modern adversaries often pursue data and other value after compromise.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — perimeter filtering is a control, not a post-compromise behavior; B — static inspection describes packet filtering; C — correct: all listed actions exploit the victim after initial access; D — baseline auditing detects changes but does not describe the adversary’s activity.

Objective: Attack Techniques

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 75; Course MD PDF Page(s) 77; CM lines 2233-2253.
question: After an initial compromise, an adversary uses the victim’s email account to send malicious messages and uses the host’s CPU to mine cryptocurrency. Which category best describes these activities?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Require the adversary to connect to a listener on the workstation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable all outbound connections from the workstation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Depend only on a static signature for the command channel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a reverse shell or other outbound command-and-control connection.

explanation:
A listener behind NAT and an inbound-blocking firewall is difficult for an adversary to reach. A reverse shell or similar outbound C2 uses a connection direction that is more likely to be permitted.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — an inbound listener is precisely what the network blocks; B — disabling outbound traffic would prevent the proposed C2; C — a signature is a detection method, not an access design; D — correct: outbound reverse communication fits the scenario.

Objective: Attack Techniques

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 82; Course MD PDF Page(s) 84; CM lines 2377-2397.
question: A compromised workstation is behind NAT and an edge firewall that does not permit unsolicited inbound connections. The adversary still needs interactive access to direct commands. Which design is most likely to succeed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It encrypts data and demands payment to recover the decryption key.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It only enumerates open services and never changes data.

choices.label: D

The course describes ransomware as encrypting data and demanding payment to recover the key. The observed encryption and payment demand therefore match the characteristic behavior.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: it states the defining behavior; B — service enumeration alone is discovery, not ransomware; C — ransomware is not limited to a public listening-service exploit; D — logging is a defender function, not the malware’s defining action.

Objective: Attack Techniques

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 45; Course MD PDF Page(s) 47; CM lines 1442-1443.
question: A response team finds that a malicious program encrypts user data and displays a demand for payment in exchange for recovery. Which characteristic is most consistent with the course’s description of modern ransomware?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leave it installed and rely on the next vulnerability scan.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the unnecessary software or disable the unnecessary functionality.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a second perimeter firewall without changing the endpoint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accept the exposure because every application must remain enabled.

explanation:
A secure baseline contains the required components and no more. Removing unused software or disabling unnecessary functionality can reduce exposure even when no patch is available.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — rescanning documents the problem but does not remove it; B — correct: it applies the baseline principle directly; C — a new perimeter firewall does not eliminate the endpoint component; D — leaving unnecessary functionality enabled preserves avoidable attack surface.

Objective: Configuration Monitoring

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 189; Course MD PDF Page(s) 750; CM lines 23241-23266.
question: A baseline review finds an unused component installed on many endpoints. The component has no available patch and is not needed for business operations. What is the best baseline-hardening action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Real-time built-in change notification only.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Event suppression based on the device’s logging configuration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A scheduled diff of the current configuration against the previous one.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Application safelisting based on the configuration filename.

explanation:
The diff approach retrieves configurations on a routine schedule, compares the current copy with the previous copy, and reports differences. That is exactly the script’s behavior.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — real-time built-in notification is the other approach; B — suppressing logging does not compare configurations; C — correct: the current-versus-previous comparison is a diff; D — application safelisting concerns executable trust, not device configuration.

Objective: Configuration Monitoring

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.5, printed page(s) 99; Course MD PDF Page(s) 869; CM lines 26949-26957.
question: A monitoring script downloads a router configuration each night, compares it with the previous copy, and alerts when the diff is nonempty. Which change-monitoring approach is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delete the old copy so it cannot be mistaken for current state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume that no configuration change occurred.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable configuration monitoring until the router is replaced.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Alert that the expected configuration backup is stale or missing.

explanation:
A remote configuration backup avoids repeated device authentication, but the monitoring process must detect when the last backup is older than the expected threshold. A stale backup is itself a monitoring condition.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — deleting evidence makes recovery and comparison harder; B — the absence of a new copy does not prove that no change occurred; C — disabling monitoring removes the needed control; D — correct: the course specifically recommends alerting on an overdue backup.

Objective: Configuration Monitoring

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.5, printed page(s) 99; Course MD PDF Page(s) 869; CM lines 26959-26966.
question: A router normally backs up its configuration to a remote repository, but the repository has not received a new copy for longer than the organization’s threshold. What should the monitoring process do?

question: An organization enables Cisco configuration change logging and forwards the events to a remote syslog server. Which setting is specifically intended to suppress passwords in the configuration log?

question: A security team excludes routers, firewalls, and IPS appliances from continuous monitoring because they are classified as “other” devices. Why is this a security problem?

choices.label: D
choices.text: A design in which preventive and detective controls are interchangeable.

A control inventory dominated by firewalls, IPS, antivirus, proxies, and filters reflects the traditional emphasis on preventing badness. The course contrasts this with stronger detective capabilities.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — the described inventory lacks the balance and instrumentation associated with modern detection; B — prevention-heavy architecture still needs monitoring; C — correct: the listed control mix is the prevention-oriented pattern; D — prevention and detection have different purposes.

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 49; Course MD PDF Page(s) 51; CM lines 1575-1591.
question: A network map shows that nearly all of an organization’s controls are firewalls, IPSs, antivirus, proxies, and web filters, with little detective instrumentation. What architectural tendency does this most strongly indicate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Trust the perimeter and focus only on keeping outsiders out.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove preventive controls because prevention is considered impossible.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wait for an automated alert before adding any response capability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assume assets may already be compromised and strengthen detection and response.

explanation:
Assume breach treats compromise as inevitable or already possible and makes detection and response much more important. It changes architecture decisions without requiring the organization to abandon prevention.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — trusting the perimeter contradicts the assumption; B — the principle does not say to remove prevention; C — waiting for alerts is reactive and does not implement the thought experiment; D — correct: it assumes assets may be compromised and builds detection and response accordingly.

Objective: Cyber Defense Principles

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 87; Course MD PDF Page(s) 89; CM lines 2549-2560.
question: A security architect is asked to redesign monitoring for a large enterprise. Which proposal best applies the assume-breach principle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A detection-oriented architecture with instrumentation for post-exploitation activity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A larger collection of perimeter blocking rules only.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Less logging so analysts have fewer events to review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A policy of waiting for users to report suspicious behavior.

explanation:
Modern defense emphasizes detecting activity after an attacker is inside, including persistence and pivoting. The proposed instrumentation addresses the exact gap described.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: it adds the missing detective capability; B — more perimeter rules do not provide internal visibility; C — reducing logs worsens detection; D — waiting for user reports is reactive and incomplete.

Objective: Cyber Defense Principles

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 88; Course MD PDF Page(s) 90; CM lines 2578-2593.
question: A company has invested heavily in preventive tools but has almost no visibility into persistence or internal pivoting after an attacker gets inside. Which modern defense emphasis addresses this gap?

choices.text: Compliance-only log retention.

Threat hunting begins with a presumption of compromise and searches for evidence rather than waiting for a sensor to produce an alert. That matches the team’s exercise.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — patch verification checks remediation, not hidden compromise; B — correct: it is proactive detection by a hunt team; C — a reverse proxy is a network placement/control choice; D — compliance retention does not require searching for compromise.

Objective: Cyber Defense Principles

The prevention sanity check classifies controls by their predominant role. The course lists SIEM as detective, while firewall, IPS, and antivirus are listed as preventive.

Objective: Cyber Defense Principles

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 50; Course MD PDF Page(s) 52; CM lines 1614-1629.
question: During a prevention sanity check, which control should be classified primarily as detective?

choices.text: A static network ACL.

choices.text: A software inventory spreadsheet.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Endpoint Detection and Response.

explanation:
EDR generates ongoing endpoint telemetry and supports investigation and response actions such as blocking communications and isolating a compromised computer. Those functions go beyond basic prevention.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — a web filter does not provide the described endpoint investigation and isolation; B — a network ACL is not endpoint telemetry; C — an inventory spreadsheet does not perform response; D — correct: the listed capabilities are EDR functions.

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 42; Course MD PDF Page(s) 603; CM lines 18568-18580.
question: An endpoint platform continuously records system behavior, supports investigation across many computers, can block selected communications, and can isolate a compromised computer. Which capability is being described?

choices.text: Tune and maintain the telemetry so the signal-to-noise ratio remains useful.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn off the detection stream and keep only a manual response tool.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use the EDR only as a preventive antivirus replacement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove analysts from the process because EDR is fully automatic.

explanation:
EDR can provide granular detection data, including activity without known indicators, but the volume can overwhelm analysts. Care, feeding, and tuning are needed to preserve useful signal.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: tuning manages the data burden; B — discarding detection data removes EDR’s central value; C — treating EDR as only prevention ignores its purpose; D — EDR still requires analysts and operational processes.

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 43; Course MD PDF Page(s) 604; CM lines 18592-18615.
question: An EDR deployment produces detailed telemetry that is valuable for detecting previously unknown indicators, but analysts are overwhelmed by its volume. What operational practice is most important?

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.text: It limits the endpoint to hash-based malware detection.

Staging EDR before an incident gives responders endpoint data and remote-action capability without waiting to deploy an investigation toolkit after discovery. That can preserve time and evidence.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — EDR improves detection and response but does not guarantee prevention; B — correct: it describes the advantage of advance deployment; C — EDR complements rather than eliminates network monitoring; D — EDR is not limited to hashes.

Objective: Device Monitoring

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 43; Course MD PDF Page(s) 604; CM lines 18608-18615.

The course treats endpoint firewall blocks and logs as valuable detection data, including evidence of attempted pivoting or egress C2. The event should be investigated rather than discarded.

Objective: Discovery and Vulnerability Scanning

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.5, printed page(s) 51; Course MD PDF Page(s) 821; CM lines 25580-25606.

Objective: Discovery and Vulnerability Scanning

question: A defender wants to identify operating systems from packet captures without actively probing the endpoints. Which tool is the course’s canonical passive OS-detection example?

choices.text: It can be the first filtering and monitoring point for inbound traffic and the last such point for outbound traffic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It can inspect every application payload without any additional device or configuration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It makes endpoint monitoring unnecessary because all attacks must stop at the router.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It can identify the user’s intent from a packet header alone.

question: A router sits at the boundary between an enterprise and an external network. Which monitoring and protection opportunity does its placement provide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: NetFlow records complete payloads and therefore replaces packet capture for content analysis.

question: A review of an enterprise map shows that more than 80% of the marked controls are primarily preventive, while internal activity is rarely investigated. Which improvement best follows the course’s cyber-defense guidance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use ATT&CK as a catalog of approved malware filenames

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use ATT&CK only to rank vulnerability scanner severity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use ATT&CK only to document encryption algorithms

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use ATT&CK for a behavior-focused defensive gap assessment

explanation:
ATT&CK is behavior-focused and can be used to assess tools, monitoring, and mitigations against adversary behavior. That makes a defensive gap assessment the best fit for comparing cloud controls by what they cover.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — ATT&CK is not primarily a filename catalog; B — it is not a replacement for asset-specific vulnerability risk decisions; C — it is not an encryption standard; D — correct: defensive gap assessment compares coverage against adversary behaviors.

Objective: Threat Informed Defense

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 102; Course MD PDF Page(s) 104; CM lines 2995-3014.
question: A security architect wants to compare two cloud products by the adversary behaviors they help protect, detect, or respond to, rather than by vendor marketing names. Which use of MITRE ATT&CK best fits this need?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the edge router for simple boundary filtering and IPFIX/NetFlow visibility

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a WAF on the router to interpret custom application logic

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use an endpoint HIDS as the router’s replacement for outbound flow data

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use split-namespace DNS as the router’s primary traffic sensor

explanation:
The router is positioned at the traditional perimeter, giving it an early inbound and late outbound vantage point. IPFIX/NetFlow supplies session-level information useful for profiling abnormal, persistent, and high-volume outbound flows.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: this combines the router’s location with its useful flow visibility; B — WAF application inspection belongs at the web-application layer; C — an endpoint HIDS cannot replace the router’s boundary view; D — split DNS addresses namespace design, not general traffic monitoring.

Objective: Perimeter Protection Devices

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.2, printed page(s) 20-21; Course MD PDF Page(s) 208-209; CM lines 6430-6482.
question: A network team wants early visibility into inbound traffic and a practical vantage point for spotting unusual, persistent outbound connections from internal systems. Which placement and capability best fit the router’s security role?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A stateful perimeter firewall by itself

choices.label: B
choices.text: Security Onion with its NIDS, HIDS, PCAP, and SIEM-related components

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nmap used as the organization’s event correlation platform

choices.label: D
choices.text: A WAF configured only for virtual patching

explanation:
Security Onion is described as an open-source NSM platform that combines network events from Zeek and Suricata, host events from agents such as Wazuh, PCAP import, and SIEM-related capabilities.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — a firewall is only one control and does not provide the described integrated NSM platform; B — correct: Security Onion combines the requested data sources and analysis functions; C — Nmap is primarily discovery/scanning; D — a WAF focuses on web applications rather than broad NSM collection.

Objective: Network Security Monitoring Tools

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.3, printed page(s) 17; Course MD PDF Page(s) 376; CM lines 11810-11836.
question: A small SOC wants one open platform that can collect network events, host events, and packet captures for hunting and investigation. Which choice best matches the course description?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A NIPS only stores packets and never changes traffic

choices.label: B
choices.text: A NIDS always causes an outage when it raises a false positive

choices.label: C
choices.text: A false positive in prevention mode can interrupt service, so NIPS tuning must be stricter

choices.label: D
choices.text: An NGFW is fundamentally limited to Layer 3 and Layer 4 filtering

explanation:
NIDS and NIPS can use the same appliance, but their configurations have different consequences. A false positive in a prevention deployment can block legitimate traffic and cause a self-inflicted outage.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — NIPS is preventive, not merely a read-only archive; B — NIDS false positives are generally an annoyance rather than an automatic outage; C — correct: prevention-mode false positives can cause service disruption; D — NGFWs are distinguished by deeper Layer 7 capabilities, not limited to Layers 3 and 4.

Objective: NIDS/NIPS/NGFW

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.2, printed page(s) 94; Course MD PDF Page(s) 282; CM lines 8792-8809.
question: A manager proposes putting an identical sensor into prevention mode because “the hardware is the same, so the risk is the same.” Which distinction should guide the decision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ingest every available event without prioritization

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace all analysts with longer data-retention periods

choices.label: C
choices.text: Treat storage capacity as the organization’s detection process

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add contextualized use cases, analysis, and a response workflow

explanation:
SIEM value is not achieved by simply collecting events. The course presents detection and response as requiring people, tools, contextual analysis, and action against the resulting intelligence.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — indiscriminate collection can worsen overload; B — retention does not substitute for analysis; C — storage is not a detection process; D — correct: use cases, analysis, and response turn collected data into security value.

Objective: Proxies & SIEM

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.3, printed page(s) 33; Course MD PDF Page(s) 392; CM lines 12303-12324.
question: An organization has centralized millions of events, but analysts still cannot identify useful signals or coordinate action. Which SIEM improvement is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clients must trust the proxy’s root CA while the proxy creates a second HTTPS connection to the server

choices.label: B
choices.text: The IDS only needs the web server’s private key and can passively decrypt every TLS 1.3 session

choices.label: C
choices.text: DNSSEC must be disabled so the proxy can see the HTTP payload

choices.label: D
choices.text: Seeing destination port 443 is sufficient to recover the application data

explanation:
Active TLS interception places the proxy in the connection path. The client establishes HTTPS with the proxy, the proxy establishes a separate HTTPS connection with the server, and clients must trust the proxy’s root CA.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: client trust and the two-leg proxy design are required; B — a server private key is associated with passive inspection and does not make passive TLS 1.3 decryption universal; C — DNSSEC is unrelated to recovering HTTP content; D — port 443 does not prove that payload data is visible.

Objective: Network Data Encryption

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.2, printed page(s) 60; Course MD PDF Page(s) 248; CM lines 7781-7793.
question: A company needs to inspect employee HTTPS traffic through an authorized internal proxy. Which condition is required for active TLS interception?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Match only the payload’s original filename

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use protocol-behavior and anomaly-oriented analysis alongside signatures

choices.label: C
choices.text: Permit all traffic that uses an established TCP session

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replace packet analysis with a static list of destination ports

explanation:
Signature matching is effective for known, stable patterns but is weaker against new, polymorphic, and custom malware. Protocol-behavior and anomaly-oriented methods add visibility into activity that does not match a known signature.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — a changed filename is easily avoided and does not describe the traffic; B — correct: behavior and anomaly methods address unknown or changing patterns; C — an established session does not make the content benign; D — ports alone do not provide sufficient exploit analysis.

Objective: Exploit Methodology and Analysis

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.3, printed page(s) 49-50; Course MD PDF Page(s) 408-409; CM lines 12843-12878.
question: A NIDS detects a known exploit reliably but misses a customized, polymorphic payload. Which detection approach should the team add to improve analysis of the unknown behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A periodic asset spreadsheet review

choices.label: B
choices.text: A perimeter router’s basic inbound filter

choices.label: C
choices.text: Endpoint Detection and Response with centralized telemetry and response actions

choices.label: D
choices.text: A one-time scan of the workload’s listening ports

explanation:
EDR continuously generates system-behavior telemetry and supports investigation and response actions, including blocking communication and isolating a compromised computer. That matches the hybrid-cloud workload’s needs.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — an asset spreadsheet does not supply live behavior or response; B — an inbound router filter lacks endpoint investigation and isolation; C — correct: EDR covers telemetry, investigation, and response; D — a one-time port scan does not provide ongoing endpoint evidence.

Objective: Device Monitoring

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 42-43; Course MD PDF Page(s) 603-604; CM lines 18568-18615.
question: A hybrid-cloud Windows workload may be compromised even though the endpoint prevention stack is enabled. The SOC needs telemetry, investigation, and the ability to isolate the host. Which capability best fits?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leave its logging disabled because the firewall is preventive

choices.label: B
choices.text: Record only inbound internet denials and discard local events

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replace endpoint logs with a monthly vulnerability report

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable and centralize endpoint firewall connection logs for detective use

explanation:
Endpoint firewalls are preventive controls, but their connection logs can provide valuable detection data. The course specifically identifies blocked connections as useful for detecting pivot attempts and egress blocking as a possible C2 signal.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — leaving logging disabled discards detective value; B — restricting collection to inbound denials misses the cited internal and outbound signals; C — a vulnerability report does not show connection attempts; D — correct: enable and centralize endpoint firewall logs for detection.

Objective: HIDS/HIPS/Endpoint Firewalls

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 44; Course MD PDF Page(s) 605; CM lines 18623-18645.
question: An organization lacks a commercial EDR platform but wants endpoint evidence of attempted lateral movement and command-and-control connections. Which action best uses the endpoint firewall?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Investigate the unexpected sensitive privilege assignment, including the account and privilege details

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ignore it because service accounts cannot be targeted by adversaries

choices.label: C
choices.text: Treat the account name as proof that the privilege is authorized

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rotate the account password and discard the privilege event

explanation:
Sensitive privileges are associated with Event ID 4672 when assigned during a logon. The course recommends monitoring the event when the subject is not a known, expected principal or when a particular privilege should be tightly limited.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: the account, subject, and granted privilege require review; B — service accounts can be targeted and abused; C — an account name does not prove the privilege is appropriate; D — password rotation alone does not explain or remediate the privilege assignment.

Objective: Account & Privilege Monitoring & Authentication

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 124; Course MD PDF Page(s) 685; CM lines 21173-21207.
question: A service account unexpectedly receives SeDebugPrivilege during logon. Which monitoring response is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Review only the board’s approval tickets at the end of the quarter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compare routine configuration snapshots and alert on security-relevant differences

choices.label: C
choices.text: Monitor only the router’s CPU utilization

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replace configuration monitoring with a single initial baseline

explanation:
Configuration monitoring compares key system state over time and alerts on security-relevant changes. A scheduled snapshot-and-diff process can reveal changes that never reached or were not authorized by the change-control board.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — quarterly ticket review is too indirect and can miss bypassed changes; B — correct: routine diffs reveal unauthorized or unexpected state changes; C — CPU usage does not describe configuration; D — a one-time baseline cannot detect later drift.

Objective: Configuration Monitoring

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 192-193; Course MD PDF Page(s) 753-754; CM lines 23351-23404.
question: A change-control board approved a router change, but the SOC also wants to detect an unauthorized change that bypasses the board. Which control best supports that goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keep a one-time manual checklist and rebuild the image only after an incident

choices.label: B
choices.text: Treat a vulnerability scan report as the hardened image

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a CIS Hardened Image as a starting point, then tailor and maintain it for the organization

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable baseline controls so the image works for every possible workload

explanation:
CIS Hardened Images use CIS Benchmarks as their foundation and provide a maintained starting point; the organization still must tailor the image to its own needs and keep it current.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — a one-time checklist does not provide a maintained deployment image; B — a scan reports vulnerabilities but does not create a hardened image; C — correct: the course presents CIS Hardened Images as a maintained, benchmark-based starting point that can be tailored; D — removing baseline controls defeats the image’s security purpose.

Objective: Patching & Secure Baseline Configurations

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 197; Course MD PDF Page(s) 758; CM lines 23523-23537.
question: A cloud platform team wants a deployment-ready operating-system image that starts from a CIS Benchmark but is tailored to the organization and updated as the benchmark and patches change. Which approach best fits?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Start with the entire production address space during peak hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scan first and request written approval after the results arrive

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trust the scanner because discovery traffic cannot affect services

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obtain written permission, test first, and use an approved maintenance window with limited scope

explanation:
Active scanning can crash systems or services, especially fragile legacy systems. The course requires written permission, testing, an approved maintenance window, and a gradual increase in scope.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — a full peak-hour scan maximizes operational risk; B — permission must precede scanning; C — discovery traffic can affect systems and services; D — correct: authorization, testing, maintenance timing, and limited scope control the risk.

Objective: Discovery and Vulnerability Scanning

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.5, printed page(s) 51; Course MD PDF Page(s) 821; CM lines 25580-25606.
question: A security engineer plans to run active discovery across a production network containing fragile legacy systems. Which preparation best follows the course guidance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Evaluate path, hash, publisher, or digital signature rather than trusting the filename alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Allow it because the filename matches a known Windows executable

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trust every executable in a user-writable directory after inventorying it once

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable application control because filenames can be spoofed

explanation:
Application-control matching can use folder, filename, path, SHA256 hash, publisher, and digital signature. A filename alone is weak because malware can imitate the name of a legitimate system binary.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: combine stronger identity attributes rather than trusting the name; B — a matching name does not make the file authentic; C — a user-writable path is not a trust anchor; D — disabling the control removes the protection instead of improving it.

Objective: Software Inventories and Application Control

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 75; Course MD PDF Page(s) 636; CM lines 19666-19697.
question: Malware is renamed to svchost.exe and placed in a user-writable directory. Which application-control decision is strongest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A SOC is simply a larger archive with more storage

choices.label: B
choices.text: A SIEM can support a SOC, but a SOC also requires people and processes for detection and response

choices.label: C
choices.text: A SOC is defined by the brand of its central console

choices.label: D
choices.text: A SOC only performs compliance reporting and never responds to incidents

explanation:
The course explicitly distinguishes a SIEM from a SOC. A SIEM can be a significant SOC component, but a SOC requires the capability to use data for detection, response, correlation, and coordinated security management.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — data storage alone is not operations; B — correct: a SIEM is a supporting system, not the complete SOC; C — a console brand does not define a SOC; D — response is a stated SOC purpose, not excluded from it.

Objective: Security Architecture Overview

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.5, printed page(s) 169-170; Course MD PDF Page(s) 939-940; CM lines 29008-29040.
question: Executives call a searchable console containing firewall, endpoint, and cloud logs “the SOC.” Which correction is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The final actions-on-objectives repository

choices.label: B
choices.text: A passive OS-detection sensor

choices.label: C
choices.text: A beachhead used for pivoting and lateral movement

choices.label: D
choices.text: A perimeter router performing inbound filtering

explanation:
The first client-side victim often serves as a beachhead or point of presence. The adversary uses the trusted internal vantage point to pivot toward systems containing the desired data.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — the laptop is not necessarily the data repository or final objective; B — it is a compromised endpoint, not a passive sensor; C — correct: it provides a bridge for pivoting; D — router filtering is a network-device function, not the laptop’s role.

Objective: Attack Techniques

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 77; Course MD PDF Page(s) 79; CM lines 2303-2320.
question: An attacker compromises a laptop that has little sensitive data, then uses it to reach a more trusted server. What role is the laptop serving in this campaign?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Internal systems are trusted, so internal monitoring adds little value

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume breach means removing all preventive controls

choices.label: C
choices.text: The organization should wait for a third party to report compromise

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assuming assets may already be compromised makes detection and response more important

explanation:
The assume-breach principle treats compromise as inevitable or already present and asks whether the architecture would be built differently. That assumption elevates the importance of detecting and responding to internal activity.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — the principle rejects treating internal assets as automatically safe; B — it does not eliminate prevention; C — waiting for third-party notification is evidence of weak internal detection; D — correct: assume breach changes the architecture toward detection and response.

Objective: Cyber Defense Principles

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 87; Course MD PDF Page(s) 89; CM lines 2549-2569.
question: A board asks why the organization should instrument internal systems when its preventive controls are strong. Which answer best reflects the assume-breach principle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adversary Emulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cyber Threat Intelligence Enrichment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Defensive Gap Assessment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Asset Inventory Reconciliation

explanation:
Adversary Emulation is an ATT&CK use case in which a team uses adversary behaviors and techniques to model an adversary and exercise the organization’s ability to detect and withstand that activity.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: the course lists Adversary Emulation as an ATT&CK use case; B — Cyber Threat Intelligence Enrichment adds behavior context to intelligence and reporting rather than describing the exercise itself; C — Defensive Gap Assessment maps coverage gaps and prioritizes improvements rather than primarily modeling an adversary exercise; D — asset inventory reconciliation concerns identifying and comparing systems, not ATT&CK-based adversary testing.

Objective: Threat Informed Defense

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 102; Course MD PDF Page(s) 104; CM lines 3002-3008.
question: A red team plans an exercise by selecting ATT&CK techniques that reflect a known adversary’s behavior and using them to test whether the organization’s controls detect and withstand that behavior. Which ATT&CK use case best describes this activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stateful inspection ignores all TCP flags and allows every ACK

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stateful inspection checks the packet against a connection state created by preceding traffic

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stateful inspection operates only at Layer 7 and cannot track TCP sessions

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stateful inspection relies on DNSSEC to validate the ACK

explanation:
A stateful firewall records the initial outbound connection and permits the corresponding response. A static filter evaluates the response packet without that connection context, so merely seeing an ACK is not equivalent.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — stateful inspection does not allow every ACK; B — correct: it validates the packet against the state table; C — stateful inspection is not limited to Layer 7; D — DNSSEC does not establish TCP connection state.

Objective: Perimeter Protection Devices

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.2, printed page(s) 24; Course MD PDF Page(s) 212; CM lines 6558-6571.
question: A static firewall sees an ACK packet but has no record of an earlier outbound SYN. Which statement best explains why a stateful inspection firewall handles this situation differently?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Compare the endpoint’s inventory spreadsheet with the certificate issuer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run an active port scan against the remote server

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Wireshark’s Follow TCP Stream to inspect the sequence of exchanged data

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the endpoint’s application-control safelist

explanation:
Following a TCP stream lets the analyst review the ordered content exchanged on the socket. The course uses this approach to expose a suspicious payload that precedes a delayed TLS exchange.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — a certificate issuer does not reveal the full byte sequence; B — an active scan changes the question and can be disruptive; C — correct: Follow TCP Stream reconstructs the conversation for inspection; D — application control does not analyze packet order.

Objective: Network Security Monitoring Tools

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.3, printed page(s) 162-163; Course MD PDF Page(s) 521-522; CM lines 15995-16022.
question: An analyst needs to determine whether a TCP stream labeled HTTPS carried a payload before the TLS handshake. Which tool action is most useful for the first review?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A static Layer 3 ACL based only on destination IP

choices.label: B
choices.text: A traditional firewall rule based only on TCP port

choices.label: C
choices.text: A NIPS rule that can never inspect application behavior

choices.label: D
choices.text: An NGFW with Layer 7 application identification and inspection

explanation:
NGFWs are built to understand Layer 7 characteristics and can identify applications and application capabilities beyond IP addresses and ports. That is the needed distinction for a collaboration application’s upload feature.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — an IP ACL cannot identify the application feature; B — a port rule cannot distinguish two applications using the same web port; C — a NIPS can have protocol and application analysis, so the claim is too broad; D — correct: NGFW application inspection supplies the required depth.

Objective: NIDS/NIPS/NGFW

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.2, printed page(s) 98-99; Course MD PDF Page(s) 286-287; CM lines 8916-8961.
question: A security team wants to distinguish a collaboration application’s file-upload feature from another application even when both use common web ports. Which control is best suited to that requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A secure web gateway that forces users through cloud-hosted inspection and filtering

choices.label: B
choices.text: A DMZ NIDS placed only in front of the office firewall

choices.label: C
choices.text: A WAF that protects the organization’s custom web applications

choices.label: D
choices.text: A local switch CAM table used as a web proxy

explanation:
The secure web gateway model routes users’ internet application connections through cloud-native or cloud-hosted inspection and filtering, including users outside the office.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: an SWG provides location-independent web control; B — an office NIDS cannot force or inspect every remote user’s web traffic; C — a WAF protects web applications rather than general employee browsing; D — a CAM table maps network attachment, not web usage.

Objective: Proxies & SIEM

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.2, printed page(s) 14; Course MD PDF Page(s) 202; CM lines 6210-6228.
question: Employees work from home and bypass the on-premises perimeter. The organization still wants consistent web filtering and inspection regardless of location. Which architecture best fits?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DoH/DoT provide query confidentiality; DNSSEC provides origin authentication and integrity without confidentiality

choices.label: B
choices.text: DNSSEC encrypts queries; DoH and DoT only sign responses

choices.label: C
choices.text: DoH and DoT provide no confidentiality unless the DNS server is authoritative

choices.label: D
choices.text: DNSSEC and DoH provide the same security properties

explanation:
DoH and DoT hide DNS queries and replies from ordinary network captures. DNSSEC authenticates the origin and integrity of responses but leaves queries and responses plaintext, so it does not provide privacy.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: the two technologies provide different security properties; B — DNSSEC does not encrypt queries; C — DoH and DoT are specifically confidentiality mechanisms; D — the properties are not identical.

Objective: Network Data Encryption

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.2, printed page(s) 147; Course MD PDF Page(s) 335; CM lines 10560-10580.
question: A cloud team wants privacy for DNS queries, while a separate integrity requirement asks defenders to know which DNS server supplied an unmodified answer. Which pairing is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Low entropy proves the strings are benign

choices.label: B
choices.text: High entropy identifies the exact malware family without additional evidence

choices.label: C
choices.text: High entropy is a useful signal for random generation, but it is not by itself proof of maliciousness

choices.label: D
choices.text: Entropy analysis replaces all packet and endpoint telemetry

explanation:
Malware and testing tools may generate random-looking names to avoid simple signatures. High entropy can identify candidates for investigation, but benign random data can also produce the signal.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — low entropy does not prove benignness; B — entropy does not identify an exact family by itself; C — correct: entropy is a useful analytic signal with limitations; D — it complements rather than replaces other telemetry.

Objective: Exploit Methodology and Analysis

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.3, printed page(s) 107; Course MD PDF Page(s) 466; CM lines 14575-14588.
question: A defender notices long, random-looking domain labels and executable names across several hosts. What is the most appropriate interpretation of the entropy signal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable process logging to reduce event volume

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rely only on the parent process name in the asset inventory

choices.label: C
choices.text: Collect only DNS responses from the perimeter router

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable full command-line auditing or Sysmon process telemetry and forward it for analysis

explanation:
Full command-line auditing and Sysmon process telemetry add the details that a bare process name lacks. Sysmon can also log process creation, network connections, and hashes, providing context for investigation.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — disabling process logging removes the needed evidence; B — a parent name alone does not reveal the command; C — DNS data lacks the process and command context; D — correct: detailed process telemetry closes the visibility gap.

Objective: Device Monitoring

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 58-59; Course MD PDF Page(s) 619-620; CM lines 19091-19155.
question: A SOC sees only “powershell.exe” in process events and cannot determine whether the command downloaded a payload. Which endpoint-monitoring improvement best addresses the gap?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It supports stateful filtering and egress controls, while its local logs must be enabled and collected for centralized use

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a cloud-only WAF that cannot log endpoint connections

choices.label: C
choices.text: It automatically performs full intrusion detection without an external analysis tool

choices.label: D
choices.text: It blocks all outbound traffic by default and therefore needs no tuning

explanation:
Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security provides stateful filtering and egress capabilities, but local logging is not enough for a SOC unless it is enabled and collected. The course notes that default logging is disabled and lacks built-in centralized collection.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: enable the logs and forward them for analysis; B — WDFAS is an endpoint firewall, not a cloud WAF; C — it does not automatically provide full intrusion detection without external analysis; D — outbound blocking and logging require configuration rather than being complete by default.

Objective: HIDS/HIPS/Endpoint Firewalls

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 24-26; Course MD PDF Page(s) 585-587; CM lines 17914-18002.
question: A Windows endpoint must both restrict egress and provide evidence of blocked pivot attempts. Which statement best describes Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The process always has full domain-administrator privileges

choices.label: B
choices.text: The administrator account’s process runs with reduced privileges until explicitly elevated

choices.label: C
choices.text: UAC changes the account’s group membership to standard user

choices.label: D
choices.text: The process cannot be elevated under any circumstance

explanation:
With UAC enabled, an account may belong to administrators while ordinary processes run with reduced privileges. Explicit elevation is required when the application needs the additional rights.

Objective: Configuration Monitoring

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.4, printed page(s) 199; Course MD PDF Page(s) 760; CM lines 23586-23608.
question: A hybrid environment requires a declared configuration state and alerts when systems drift from it. Which capability best fits?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a patching solution covering OS and third-party updates and audit compliance routinely

Objective: Patching & Secure Baseline Configurations

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.5, printed page(s) 54; Course MD PDF Page(s) 824; CM lines 25642-25674.
question: Two authorized Nmap scans of a critical server network show that three ports appeared between runs. Which tool is designed to highlight that change?

Application control begins with a known-good inventory and safelist. Anything outside that list should at least require exception handling, including investigation of how the binary arrived and why it is executing.

Objective: Software Inventories and Application Control

question: An application-control agent encounters an executable that is absent from the known-good inventory. What should the workflow do first?

The current-state discussion accepts that even robust prevention can fail. Continuous Security Monitoring supplies the detection capability needed to respond to the next unforeseen threat.

Objective: Security Architecture Overview

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 6; Course MD PDF Page(s) 8; CM lines 187-214.
question: A company has strong perimeter prevention but little capability to detect an attacker who bypasses it. Which architecture change best follows the course’s current-state assessment?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Combine network metadata and host monitoring because encryption makes network inspection more difficult

Modern adversaries increasingly encrypt exfiltration and C2, creating network blind spots. The course therefore calls for more monitoring on the host while still using available network evidence.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — encryption protects content from easy inspection but does not make the activity harmless; B — exfiltration is outbound, so inbound-only monitoring misses it; C — a single TLS signature cannot address encrypted host behavior; D — correct: host telemetry and network metadata complement each other.

choices.label: D

Threat hunting is proactive detection. Hunt teams begin with a presumption of compromise and search for evidence rather than waiting for an automated alert to identify it.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — correct: proactive searching is the defining behavior; B — compliance review is not threat hunting; C — removing automated detections discards useful evidence; D — restricting hunting to the perimeter misses post-exploitation activity.

Objective: Cyber Defense Principles

Source: GIAC GMON / SEC511, Book 511.1, printed page(s) 89; Course MD PDF Page(s) 91; CM lines 2599-2629.
question: A hunt team is asked to wait for alerts from existing sensors before investigating possible compromise. Which operating model best reflects proactive threat hunting?

question: An Azure control-mapping layer shows that a native control covers a technique. Before treating the technique as adequately defended, what should the defender verify?

question: A team wants a temporary installation that can receive live traffic from a TAP or SPAN port while evaluating Security Onion features. Which architecture is appropriate?

choices.text: NIDS always encrypts internal traffic before analysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: The switch CAM table automatically suppresses all internal events

Traditional IDS configurations commonly distinguish trusted and untrusted segments. A pivot from one trusted internal host to another can be treated as innocuous when the rules focus on untrusted-to-trusted attacks.

choices.text: A packet-capture archive with no filtering

Virtual patching uses a WAF to block exploitation attempts against a known flaw before the custom code is fixed. It is a temporary mitigation, not a substitute for correcting the application.

choices.text: Passive decryption will work if the client trusts the IDS certificate

choices.label: D

Passive TLS inspection with a server RSA private key depends on the key-establishment model and does not work when forward secrecy is used. The course identifies TLS 1.3 as requiring forward secrecy, so an active proxy or endpoint telemetry is needed instead.

question: An IDS has the RSA private key for an internal web server, but the server now requires TLS 1.3 with forward secrecy. Which result should the analyst expect?

choices.text: Review only inbound-denied internet traffic from the perimeter

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inventory persistent external connections from firewall, proxy, or PCAP-summary data and investigate unknown ones

Persistent connections from internal systems to less-trusted external systems are a cornerstone NSM detection target. Firewall, proxy, and PCAP-summary data can reveal connections that remain active or recur continuously.

choices.text: A quarterly hardware inventory with no process data

choices.text: A router’s static inbound ACL counters only

Full command-line logging makes Event ID 4688 much more useful for identifying encoded or otherwise suspicious PowerShell activity. The event is high volume and may expose sensitive values, so it should be filtered or post-processed carefully.

question: A response team wants to distinguish a legitimate PowerShell launch from a long, encoded post-exploitation command. Which event source is especially useful, with an important operational caveat?

choices.text: Put all three applications on the organization-wide allow list

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use host-based firewall application rules to block or alert on those applications where they are not needed

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable endpoint firewall logging to avoid false positives

choices.label: D
choices.text: Permit the applications whenever their filenames match the safelist

Host-based firewalls can filter by application as well as by port and address. Blocking or alerting on tools such as PowerShell, PsExec, and WMIC where non-IT users do not need them can expose attempted lateral movement.

Why the other choices are wrong: A — allowing the applications everywhere expands the attack surface; B — correct: application rules can restrict and detect inappropriate use; C — disabling logs removes the evidence; D — a filename match alone is not sufficient authorization.

question: Non-IT workstations should not allow PowerShell remoting, PsExec, or WMIC to communicate freely. Which endpoint control use is most appropriate?

choices.text: Pass-the-hash used for lateral movement with reused local credentials

choices.label: D
choices.text: DNS cache poisoning caused by a split namespace

Pass-the-hash uses a compromised NTLM hash to authenticate where the same username and hash are accepted. Unsalted hashes and synchronized local administrator credentials increase the opportunity for lateral movement.

choices.label: D

CIS Benchmarks provide vendor-neutral baseline guidance developed through industry consensus. The organization should use that established starting point and adapt it after testing required functionality.

question: A regulated organization needs long-term storage for compliance and post-mortem review, but the SOC also needs near-real-time, enriched intrusion detection. Which SIEM design best addresses both needs?

question: A company has enough endpoint, network, and cloud telemetry to overwhelm a small team. What is the primary technical purpose of a SOC that would help?
